Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Pravesh Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned AGA for the State.

2. Present application u/s 482 of Cr PC has been filed by the applicants, praying for quashing the summoning order dated 6.11.2023 passed by First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rampur in Complaint Case No.458 of 2022 (Smt. Bijness vs. Bhoop Singh and others) under Sections 323, 406,
494, 504, 506 of IPC against applicant no.1 and under Sections 323, 406, 504, 506 of IPC against the applicant nos.2 to 7, Police Station Shahbad, District Rampur, as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No.458 of 2022 (Smt. Bijness vs. Bhoop Singh and others) under Sections 323, 406,
494, 504, 506 of IPC against applicant no.1 and under Sections 323, 406, 504, 506 of IPC against the applicant nos.2 to 7, Police Station Shahbad, District Rampur.

sentences.text: Kajal was taken away by her family members on the pretext that she will return within a week and Kajal has also taken Rs.3.5 lacs along with jewellery with her, but when she did not return to her matrimonial house, opposite party no.2 and her son went to find out her daughter-in-law, namely Kajal.
On 20.8.2022, her son came to know that Kajal has solemnized her marriage with one Ankush in the pressure of her family members.
After recording the primary evidence under Sections 200 and 202 of Cr PC, the learned Magistrate summoned the applicants to face trial.

4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the entire prosecution story is false,
fabricated and fictitious.

Even the complaint filed by opposite party no.2 is full of contradiction because the affidavit in support of the complaint was prepared on 19.5.2021, whereas the complaint has been filed on 20.9.2022.

Applicant no.2-Bhoop Singh lodged an FIR, having Crime No.370 of 2021 under Section 366 of IPC against the son of opposite party no.2 on 3.8.2021 in which, after investigation, a charge-sheet came to be filed against the son of opposite party no.2 under Sections 366, 328, 376 of IPC on 12.4.2022.

A similar FIR, having Crime No.305 of 2023 was also lodged against the son of opposite party no.2 under Sections 363 and 366 of IPC on 13.12.2023.
5.

It has been argued on behalf of the applicants that the present complaint has been lodged by opposite party no.2 with malicious intention, just to mount pressure upon Kajal and her family members for compromise in the matter.
Opposite party no.2 has no locus to lodge the present complaint, as she is not an aggrieved party.
Present proceedings are initiated as a counter blast.

It has been further argued that the case of the applicants is covered under Section 198 of Cr PC.
6.
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer and submitted that the impugned summoning order has been passed on the basis of primary evidence available on record and there is no infirmity in the same.

7. Considering the rival submission of learned counsel for the parties as well as the material available on record, this Court finds that the learned Magistrate, after perusing the statements of the complainant as well as the witnesses, has summoned the applicants to face trial.
So far as the contentions raised by the applicants are concerned, they can very well be raised before the trial Court by moving an appropriate discharge application.

8. Therefore, present application is disposed of, with a direction to the applicants to move an appropriate discharge application before the trial Court, within two months from today, which shall be considered and decided by the trial Court expeditiously in accordance with law, after affording an opportunity of hearing to the parties.
9. For a period of 60 days from today or till the disposal of discharge application, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforementioned case.

Order Date :- 15.5.2024 RKK/-
